TITLE: Convergence guarantees for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: We prove non-asymptotic sample-complexity guarantees for KernelSHAP, assuming that the value function v(S) is L-smooth, i.e. ∇v(S) ≤ L for all S ⊆ [d]. We derive the sample complexity bounds for the estimator, depending on the L, the total variation distance between the empirical and true value functions, and a combinatorial term related to the kernel weights.
CONTROLS: We compare our bounds to the known asymptotic guarantees for unbiased KernelSHAP and show that our result is tighter in low-noise regimes. 
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Our bound shows that KernelSHAP with O((dlogd)/ε^2) samples is sufficient to achieve ε-accuracy, which can be compared to the informed upper bound of O((d^2)log(d)/ε^2) derived from the asymptotic analysis of unbiased KernelSHAP.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Empirical comparison of LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: We conduct a wide range of experiments to compare the performance of LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP on real-world datasets in various domains, including image classification, natural language processing, and tabular data. We evaluate the accuracy and stability of the two estimators under different sampling distributions and choice of kernels. We also investigate how the dimensionality of the input affects their performance.
CONTROLS: We use SHAP's own implementation of KernelSHAP and a modified version of LeverageSHAP to compare the two estimators. We include T-statistic based baseline by reverting back to the also widely used LIME for comparison and ablation studies to highlight the implications of kernel selection on the Shapley values. 
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: Our experiment will demonstrate the asymptotic convergence properties of LeverageSHAP, and we anticipate a similar performance with KernelSHAP unless its kernel choice remains suboptimal in our high-dimensional setting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable implementation of LeverageSHAP for high-dimensional inputs
PROPOSAL: We develop a scalable and efficient implementation of LeverageSHAP that takes advantage of parallel processing and approximation techniques to handle high-dimensional inputs. Specifically, we use importance sampling and randomized sketching to reduce the computational cost of leveraging score computation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a variety of benchmark datasets and compare its performance to existing scalable Shapley value estimators.
CONTROLS: We compare our implementation to the original LeverageSHAP and a variant of SimSHAP, which uses importance sampling, and report their trade-offs and overhead with respect to accuracy. 
COST: 60000
PREDICTION: Our implementation will achieve significant speedup over the original LeverageSHAP, achieving accuracy competitive with it on high-dimensional datasets.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Simplified implementation of scalable LeverageSHAP for high-dimensional inputs
PROPOSAL: We simplify our scalable implementation of LeverageSHAP, focusing on a more lightweight importance sampling scheme and removing the elaborate randomized sketching step. We benchmark its performance on real-world datasets and find that it offers an efficient balance between accuracy and computational resources.
CONTROLS: We compare our revised implementation to the original LeverageSHAP and a simple variant of SimSHAP, reporting their differences in terms of accuracy and execution time. 
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: Our simplified implementation will provide a faster but slightly less accurate alternative to the original LeverageSHAP, offering a more accessible solution for practitioners requiring efficient computations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring the robustness of SHAP values to noise in feature values
PROPOSAL: We investigate the sensitivity of SHAP values to noise in the input feature values by adding randomness to the training data and evaluating the resulting SHAP values. We examine how the choice of kernel and sampling distribution affects the stability of SHAP values in the presence of noise. We also compare the robustness of LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP in this scenario.
CONTROLS: We use a variety of noise generation methods, including Gaussian noise and uniform noise, and evaluate the quality of the SHAP values using the mean absolute error metric. We report the results for different levels of noise and choose of kernel and we do that for both estimators. 
COST: 40000
PREDICTION: Our experiment will reveal that LeverageSHAP exhibits better robustness to noise than KernelSHAP, especially when the noise is Gaussian, and provide insight into the relation between kernel choice and SHAP value stability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Non-asymptotic convergence analysis for SimSHAP
PROPOSAL: We derive a non-asymptotic convergence rate for SimSHAP under the assumption that the value function v(S) is Lipschitz smooth. Our result establishes a connection between the convergence rate of SimSHAP and the number of samples used in the approximation. We discuss the implications of our analysis for the practical application of SimSHAP in high-dimensional settings.
CONTROLS: We compare the convergence rate of SimSHAP to that of LeverageSHAP under the same conditions and kernel choice, showing that our analysis can be used to select the most appropriate estimator given the available amount of data. 
COST: 42000
PREDICTION: Our analysis will demonstrate that SimSHAP's convergence rate is more favorable than LeverageSHAP's in certain regimes, specifically when dealing with small values of Lipschitz constant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparison of LeverageSHAP and Gaussian process-based estimator for Shapley values
PROPOSAL: We investigate the performance of a recently proposed Gaussian process-based estimator for Shapley values and compare it to LeverageSHAP. We explore the algorithm's ability to handle high-dimensional inputs and evaluate its accuracy using a set of rigorous metrics.
CONTROLS: We compare the results of LeverageSHAP to those of the GP-based method using metrics such as mean absolute error and KL divergence, and we report the processing time and the standard deviation of the method we propose to make a thorough comparison. 
COST: 90000
PREDICTION: Our experiment will reveal that the GP-based estimator offers excellent performance, but may require overoptimistic approximation of the GP for more computational friendly approximation; in such cases LeverageSHAP may be a better fit given precision needed for analysis.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fast and adaptive importance sampling for high-dimensional Shapley values
PROPOSAL: We develop a new importance sampling strategy tailored for high-dimensional Shapley values estimation that adaptively adjusts the sampling distribution based on the underlying value function's behavior. Our method leverages a neural network to learn an approximate distribution, allowing for efficient sampling and estimating of Shapley values.
CONTROLS: We compare our strategy to the simple and previously used fixed importance sampling method implemented in KernelSHAP, reporting their differences in terms of accuracy and computational time for both estimators. 
COST: 85000
PREDICTION: Our adaptive importance sampling strategy will achieve significant improvement over the fixed sampling strategy for Shapley values estimation in high-dimensional spaces, offering considerable accuracy and efficiency gains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Shapley value estimator for neural network-based Shapley value methods
PROPOSAL: We propose a unified framework that extends the applicability of Shapley value methods to neural network-based predictors, integrating insights from existing estimators to provide a more comprehensive and effective tool for understanding neural network models.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the proposed framework against several popular methods, including KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, and compare their performances in terms of accuracy, computational efficiency and robustness to different hyperparameters and noise levels, demonstrating the capabilities of our unified framework for neural network Shapley values. 
COST: 110000
PREDICTION: Our unified framework will outperform existing methods for neural network Shapley values estimation, particularly in scenarios featuring complex neural networks and high-dimensional input spaces, as well as in cases with noisy input data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Shapley value estimation with implicit regularization using early stopping
PROPOSAL: We investigate the effectiveness of early stopping as a regularization technique for improving Shapley value estimation, aiming to prevent overfitting and selection bias while reducing computational resources. Our experiments involve applying early stopping to several popular Shapley value estimators and evaluating their performance on real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: We compare our results to the same estimators without early stopping and to alternative regularization methods, providing insights into the advantages and limitations of our proposed approach. 
COST: 120000
PREDICTION: Our use of early stopping will lead to improved performance in terms of accuracy and robustness, while reducing training time, making Shapley values estimation more manageable and reliable.

Train the model on a large-scale dataset of satellite image time series, such as the BEACHES dataset, comprising images acquired at irregular intervals over multiple years. COST: 8000
PREDICTION: This approach should significantly outperform the baseline in both tasks and improve long-range temporal understanding, enabling temporally consistent forecasts. However, model interpretability and the difficulty of the GNN in capturing complex long-term causal relationships might pose challenges.

TITLE: Transfer Learning for Temporal Change Description and Future Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Integrate a pre-trained language model, specifically the BART model, as the primary encoder for temporal change description and future forecasting tasks. Fine-tune the model on the satellite image time series dataset to adapt to the specific domain and tasks. This will leverage the language model's ability to capture long-range dependencies and semantic relationships in text, which can be beneficial for modeling temporal changes and forecasting.

PROPOSAL: Develop a multimodal fusion approach to integrate satellite imagery and text data for temporal change description and future forecasting tasks. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Update of Pretrained Forecasters for Distribution Shift
PROPOSAL: Revise the online gradient descent (OGD) update procedure to adapt only the ensemble weights of a pre-trained forecasting model, which combines the predictions of multiple temperature and input-restored neural networks. This approach is inspired by the merits of knowledge distillation and the empirical benefits of adapting ensemble weights in prior work. We update the ensemble weights once every T steps using a batch of B samples collected at the current and previous T-1 steps, with a learning rate of α that is gradually reduced as the number of updates grows.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to the standard OGD update of the entire model's parameters, as well as variants that update only the final prediction layer or a simple adapter module after the model's output. We also evaluate the robustness of our update mechanism by injecting concept drift into the environment and assessing its effect on the model's performance.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: This approach should reduce the variance of the gradient estimates and improve the model's ability to adapt to the evolving patterns in the environment, especially when faced with concept drift. However, it may not generalize as well to scenarios where the underlying relationship between the input and target variables changes more dramatically.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Benefits and Limitations of Adapting Low-Rank Scaling Coefficients
PROPOSAL: Modify the efficient update of the pretrained forecaster proposal 1 to adapt only the low-rank scaling coefficients of the model weights, as opposed to ensemble weights. This approach limits the fraction of adjusted parameters to a smaller subspace, and could further reduce the variance of the gradient estimates. To evaluate its benefits and limitations, we compare its performance against adapting the ensemble weights (proposal 1), as well as adapting the ensemble weights with an increased batch size (B) or a reduced learning rate (α).
CONTROLS: Standard OGD update of the entire model's parameters, adapting only the final prediction layer, and a simple adapter module after the model's output.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: Adapting low-rank scaling coefficients could further improve the model's adaptability to evolving patterns, but may be sensitive to its dimensionality, the model's capacity to adjust, and the changing relationship between the input and target variables.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Online Forecasting with Temporally Aggregated Statistics
PROPOSAL: Implement a horizon-adaptive approach that aggregates statistics of the data over varying time horizons and then uses this information for the forecasting process. We compute the aggregated statistics (e.g., mean, variance) recursively using the most recent H steps' data, where H is a hyperparameter. These aggregated statistics are then used as additional inputs to the pre-trained forecasting model, which generates predictions. We update the model's parameters using the efficient update procedure in proposal 1.
CONTROLS: Compare against adapting ensemble weights or low-rank scaling coefficients alone, as well as standard OGD update of the entire model's parameters.
COST: 4400
PREDICTION: The combination of the horizon-adaptive approach and the efficient update procedure should improve the model's adaptability and performance under changing data distributions. However, its effectiveness might be limited by the empirical risk minimization bias, which may lead to overfitting the aggregated statistics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluation on Traffic Flow Forecasting Domain
PROPOSAL: Apply the efficient update of pretrained forecasters for distribution shift (proposal 1), the low-rank scaling coefficients adaptation (proposal 2), and the horizon-adaptive aggregation approach (proposal 3) on the traffic flow forecasting domain. We use the real-world traffic data from Peek Traffic and CloudStrap to evaluate the performance of the proposed methods under both stationary and non-stationary conditions.
CONTROLS: Standard baseline methods for online forecasting, such as naive method, seasonal decomposition, and exponential smoothing state space model (SES).
COST: 8200
PREDICTION: These approaches should significantly outperform the standard baseline methods under both stationary and non-stationary conditions in the traffic flow forecasting domain, considering the pre-training of the deep auto-regressive model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Sensitivity of Proposed Methods to Data Frequency
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of the efficient update of pretrained forecasters for distribution shift (proposal 1), the low-rank scaling coefficients adaptation (proposal 2), and the horizon-adaptive aggregation approach (proposal 3) under different sampling frequencies, including hourly, daily, and weekly sampling. This is to investigate how these methods handle changing data frequencies and potential correlations between consecutive samples.
CONTROLS: Analyze the results under each sampling frequency and compare the performance of the proposed methods.
COST: 32000
PREDICTION: The proposed methods may still perform well under different sampling frequencies, especially those using the horizon-adaptive aggregation approach, which is designed to handle sequences with varying lengths.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Batch Selection Strategies for Efficient Update Procedure
PROPOSAL: Investigate different batch selection strategies to improve the efficiency and robustness of the efficient update procedure (proposal 1). Specifically, we consider greedy, random, and importance-weighted sampling methods for selecting the samples to be used for the update. We analyze the performance of these strategies under various scenarios, including stationary and non-stationary conditions.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of these batch selection strategies against a baseline approach that uses a uniformly sampled batch.
COST: 56000
PREDICTION: The importance-weighted sampling method is likely to outperform the other batch selection strategies, especially under non-stationary conditions, by selectively focusing on the most informative samples. However, its effectiveness may be challenged by the need to estimate the importance weights accurately.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Robust Online Forecasting with Temporally Aggregated Statistics: Improved Recursive Aggregation
PROPOSAL: Revise the horizon-adaptive aggregation approach (proposal 3) to use an improved recursive aggregation method that takes into account the temporal dependencies between consecutive samples. Specifically, we use a Gaussian process to model the temporal dynamics and update the aggregated statistics using a recursive algorithm. This revised approach is expected to improve the model's ability to handle non-stationary conditions.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the revised approach against the original horizon-adaptive aggregation approach and the efficient update procedure (proposal 1).
COST: 64000
PREDICTION: The revised horizon-adaptive aggregation approach is likely to outperform the original approach under non-stationary conditions, especially when the data exhibits strong temporal dependencies. However, it may be computationally more expensive due to the need to estimate the Gaussian process parameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Task Learning for Online Forecasting under Distribution Shift
PROPOSAL: Incorporate a multi-task learning component into the online forecasting framework to learn the underlying patterns and relationships between multiple related time series data streams. This can be achieved by sharing a common backbone network and adapting it online using the efficient update procedure (proposal 1). We evaluate the performance of this approach on multiple real-world datasets, including traffic flow, electricity consumption, and weather forecasting.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the multi-task learning approach against the single-task learning approach and the baseline methods.
COST: 80000
PREDICTION: The multi-task learning approach is likely to improve the model's ability to handle distribution shift and non-stationary conditions, especially when the related time series data streams exhibit similar patterns and correlations. However, it may be challenging to tune the hyperparameters of the multi-task learning framework.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Online Gradient Descent for Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Provide a theoretical analysis of the online gradient descent (OGD) update procedure used in the efficient update of pretrained forecasters for distribution shift (proposal 1). We derive regret bounds for OGD in the context of time series forecasting and explore the properties of the update procedure under different assumptions. Our analysis provides insights into the design of the efficient update procedure and its convergence properties.
CONTROLS: Compare the theoretical guarantees of OGD against other online learning algorithms and the limited regret bounds of other algorithms for time series forecasting.
COST: 96000
PREDICTION: The theoretical analysis will provide a solid foundation for understanding the convergence properties of the efficient update procedure and its robustness to data stream variations. However, it may be challenging to quantify the regret bounds for OGD in the context of time series forecasting, particularly when the data exhibits strong temporal dependencies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Sampling for Efficient Online Forecasting under Concept Drift
PROPOSAL: Develop an adaptive sampling strategy to efficiently select the most informative samples for online forecasting under concept drift. We combine the batch selection strategies (proposal 6) with a concept drift detection mechanism to identify the most relevant samples for updating the model. This adaptive sampling strategy is designed to improve the model's adaptability and performance under non-stationary conditions.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the adaptive sampling strategy against other sampling strategies and the baseline methods.
COST: 120000
PREDICTION: The adaptive sampling strategy is likely to improve the model's adaptability and performance under non-stationary conditions by selectively focusing on the most informative samples. However, its effectiveness may be challenged by the need to accurately detect concept drift and balance exploration and exploitation.
